claim: Café Romand on Place Saint-François is a Belle Epoque brasserie open since 1951, awarded 'Café historique de Lausanne' in 2021, serving papet vaudois, moitié-moitié fondue, and malakoffs.
quote: Café Romand sits on Place Saint-François 2 in downtown Lausanne... It's a historic brasserie with 'Belle Epoque' decor that has retained its original character since 1951... Signature dishes include 'papet vaudois', half-and-half fondue, and malakoffs.

claim: La Pinte Besson, founded in 1780, is the oldest café in Lausanne and has a vaulted cellar-bar atmosphere with a fondue with morels and cognac.
quote: Founded in 1780, Pinte Besson is the oldest café in Lausanne. The ground floor offers a fondue with morels and cognac in a cellar bar atmosphere from 1870.

claim: Time Out confirms Pinte Besson 'claims to be the oldest pub in Lausanne, and was set up by a wine merchant in 1780' and notes Brasserie de Montbenon occupies a prime spot in Montbenon park.
quote: Claims to be the oldest pub in Lausanne, and was set up by a wine merchant in 1780... Opened at the end of 2014, this stylish brasserie occupies a prime location on the classy (and grassy) Montbenon park

claim: Café du Grütli at Rue de la Mercerie 4 is a family-run Swiss restaurant specializing in fondue, seasonal Vaudois dishes, and 'La Chasse des Grisons' game menu, run by the Prutsch family.
quote: Rue de la Mercerie 4, CH-1003 Lausanne... The café specializes in traditional Swiss cuisine. They feature fondue as a signature offering, with menus highlighting 'produits frais de saison'.

claim: Café du Vieil Ouchy at Place du Port 3 is a lakeside historic café (labelled 'Café historique de Lausanne' in 2021) serving cheese fondue, Lake Geneva perch fillets, and meringues with double cream.
quote: Cheese fondue is the restaurant's signature offering. The menu also features regional dishes including cordon bleu and Lake Geneva perch fillets. The establishment is known for its desserts, particularly 'meringues with double cream'.

claim: Café de Grancy on Boulevard de Grancy below the station is a bistro doing weekend brunch (10:00–15:00 Sat/Sun), Wednesday fondue nights, and seasonal contemporary cooking with a library and terrace.
quote: Brunchs are organized every Saturday and Sunday, with service available from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM... Wednesday evenings feature fondue nights with original options... The cuisine oscillates between bistro and gastronomy, prioritizing seasons and local products.

claim: Ta Cave at Rue du Simplon 35 is Switzerland's first crowdfunded wine bar (opened 2015) with a monthly-rotating list of six to ten picks plus discovery wines, snack boards, and a Meule cheese-mould bread.
quote: Ta Cave is Switzerland's first crowdfunded wine bar... a selection of six to ten best wine picks every month and eight discovery wines... A notable specialty is 'the delicious La Meule bread, baked in cheese moulds'.

claim: Lausanne's curated wine-bar shortlist also includes Le 20 (Petit-Chêne 11), Vintage (Langallerie 7), Vinothèque du Château d'Ouchy (Place du Port), and Street Cellar in the Flon (Port-Franc 2a).
quote: Le 20 (Rue du Petit-Chêne 11)... Vintage wine bar (Rue Langallerie 7)... Vinothèque du Château d'Ouchy (Place du Port)... Ta Cave (Rue du Simplon 35)... Street Cellar (Rue du Port-Franc 2a)

claim: The Flon district concentrates bars and restaurants including King Size Pub, Les Jardins de PAM rooftop, Barberousse rum bar, Cipriano Wine & Ham, Brasserie Belleville, Forbici (Italian), and TAO lounge.
quote: Street Cellar (Wine bar) / King Size Pub (Pub with giant screen) / Les Jardins de PAM (Rooftop bar) / Barberousse (Rum bar) / Cipriano Wine & Ham (Café bar) / Brasserie Belleville / Forbici / TAO (Lounge bar-restaurant)

claim: Top Tripadvisor picks near the Cathédrale include Amici (Italian, 4.4), Brasserie Les 100 Suisses (Swiss, 4.9), Creperie la Chandeleur with a cathedral view, and Vieux-Lausanne Restaurant & Giraf Bar in the old town.
quote: Amici (4.4★) - Italian Mediterranean... Brasserie Les 100 Suisses (4.9★) - Swiss European cuisine featuring 'Very friendly service'... Creperie la Chandeleur (4.2★) - French European creperie with 'great view'... Vieux-Lausanne Restaurant & Giraf Bar (4.4★) - French and Swiss dining in a 'Historical place in old town'

claim: Lausanne Tourisme's brunch/bakery picks include Bread Store (run by 'Best Worker in France' baker Thomas Marie), Bryo 'The Brioche House', gluten/lactose-free El Gato Pâtisserie, Maison Buet, and Bel-Air Coffee.
quote: Awarded the title of Best Worker in France, baker Thomas Marie offers... Bryo, known as The Brioche House, is a new spot in Lausanne focused on... El Gato... first gluten- and lactose-free patisserie in Lausanne... Maison Buet... This artisan bakery and chocolate shop runs a café boutique

claim: The Lausanne Guide's specialty-coffee shortlist highlights Bel-Air Coffee (Scandi feel), Ça Passe Crème, Sleepy Bear (run by Diana), Bold Coffee Club in Sous-Gare, Ordinary Man on Petit-Chêne (roasted on-site), and The Coffee Project.
quote: Bel-Air Coffee: This stylish coffee shop has a Scandi feel to it... Sleepy Bear: Diana and her team's knowledge and passion about coffee permeate each cup... Bold Coffee Club: Located in sous gare... Ordinary Man Coffee: A café slash art gallery located right on Petit Chene
